question: Should this shared protocol engine and `@openclaw/gateway-client/browser` entrypoint become the canonical internal lifecycle boundary for both the Node Gateway client and Control UI at this head?
rationale: The implementation appears correct, but it centralizes security-sensitive authentication and reconnect decisions so a future shared-engine regression would affect both clients; repository policy requires explicit ownership of that boundary.

options.title: Approve the canonical boundary
options.body: Confirm the browser export is internal, wait for exact-head required checks, and merge the well-proven consolidation.

options.title: Narrow the exported surface
options.body: Keep the shared engine but avoid or explicitly mark the browser package entrypoint if maintainers do not want it to become a consumable contract.

options.title: Pause for SDK direction
options.body: Defer the package-boundary change until the public support contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49178 is decided.

recommendation.title: Approve the canonical boundary
recommendation.body: Confirm the browser export is internal, wait for exact-head required checks, and merge the well-proven consolidation.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior Gateway authentication and SDK history plus ownership of the linked consolidation issue make this person the strongest available boundary-decision owner.
